criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies the 55% equity allocation as an arithmetic error
criteria_results.reasoning: The report says the 41.07% change is 'not mere arithmetic' and does not call the Debtor's 55% an error to be corrected to 41.07%. It treats 55% as exposed but possibly defensible (the net method gives 54%).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Shows the correct waterfall math for equity allocation
criteria_results.reasoning: Section VI.E shows TEV of $407.5M less $261.4M gives REV of $146.1M, and $60M / $146.1M = 41.07%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Recommends accepting the Committee's correction to 41.07%
criteria_results.reasoning: The report expressly recommends 'Do not accept as a correction' and says to resolve the point with Timberline and Clearview.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies Committee's deletion of non-consensual third-party releases
criteria_results.reasoning: B-1 and VII.1 identify the strike of the § 10.4(c) non-consensual release and discuss its legal implications.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Analyzes enforceability under Ninth Circuit / Purdue Pharma
criteria_results.reasoning: The report cites Purdue (144 S. Ct. 2071 (2024)) and Ninth Circuit Lowenschuss, and concludes the provision cannot be defended, so the Committee's point has merit.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Recommends narrowing or eliminating non-consensual releases
criteria_results.reasoning: It recommends accepting the deletion and recasting the release as consensual.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies avoidance action proceeds allocation to unsecured creditors
criteria_results.reasoning: A-4 identifies the new Avoidance Action Recovery Pool sending 100% of net proceeds to GUCs instead of the Reorganized Debtor, with the ~$9.5M figure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Flags potential double recovery / combined recovery analysis
criteria_results.reasoning: VI.D combines the $28.0M pool with $9.5M of avoidance proceeds for $37.5M (20.05%). The structure screens treat the pool and the preference share together (e.g., $18.7M plus 50% of net preferences).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies Committee's deletion of $3.4M retention bonuses
criteria_results.reasoning: A-7 identifies the strike of the $3.4M program for 12 senior employees and the Committee's § 503(c) 'disguised priority payments' argument.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Analyzes § 503(c) requirements for retention payments
criteria_results.reasoning: VII.6 discusses § 503(c)(1) (bona fide job offer, essential services, caps) and § 503(c)(3).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Recommends preparing § 503(c) compliance evidence
criteria_results.reasoning: It recommends a § 503(c) motion with an evidentiary record, plus gathering evidence of competing offers and insider status.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies Committee's MIP reduction from 10% to 7%
criteria_results.reasoning: A-6 identifies the MIP reduction from 10% to 7%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Flags internal incoherence of MIP reduction rationale
criteria_results.reasoning: It states that GUCs receive no equity, so MIP dilution falls on Timberline and the Committee's rationale fails.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Recommends pushing back on MIP change or identifying it as leverage
criteria_results.reasoning: It recommends holding at 10% or trading the point through Timberline, and does not concede it for free.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies Committee's new cramdown reserve provision (§ 11.9)
criteria_results.reasoning: E-1 identifies new § 11.9, which applies if Class 3 rejects and invokes absolute-priority compliance under § 1129(b)(2)(B).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Links cramdown provision to retention bonuses as negotiating lever
criteria_results.reasoning: It notes that § 11.9(b) characterizes the retention program as value retained by insiders junior to GUCs. It also lists the retention record and the cramdown threat as Committee leverage.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies increased Effective Date cash requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: It identifies that the Effective Date cash need rises from $62.85M to $74.50M.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Calculates or references Effective Date cash requirements
criteria_results.reasoning: The VI.A table gives $62.85M vs. $74.50M (+$11.65M), with the components matching the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Flags feasibility concern — Committee's cash need vs. projected cash at emergence
criteria_results.reasoning: It flags a $6.5M shortfall against $68.0M of projected cash and a § 1129(a)(11) feasibility concern.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Recommends requesting feasibility analysis from Pinecrest Advisory Group
criteria_results.reasoning: It recommends that Pinecrest re-run the sources and uses and the feasibility screens before May 26.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies contract rejection standard change
criteria_results.reasoning: D-1 identifies the change from the § 8.2 business-judgment standard to a 'material net burden' standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Analyzes against § 365 / Bildisco business judgment standard
criteria_results.reasoning: It cites Bildisco as establishing the business-judgment standard for rejection and calls the Committee's test a novel heightened standard.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Recommends rejecting the contract rejection standard change
criteria_results.reasoning: It recommends rejecting the change.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies release carve-out for Timberline's 2021 dividend recap
criteria_results.reasoning: B-2 identifies the carve-out of Timberline's 2021 Dividend Recap claims from the releases, with those claims vesting in the trust.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Flags risk to Timberline's continued Plan support
criteria_results.reasoning: It flags that Timberline's support is conditioned on its treatment and that Timberline may withdraw support (the 'Timberline Support Risk').

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Recommends a negotiated compromise on Timberline releases
criteria_results.reasoning: It recommends compromise options: a limited carve-out, an independent investigation with a 9019 settlement, or a cap or standstill.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies addition of interest on deferred unsecured payments
criteria_results.reasoning: A-3 identifies interest at the federal judgment rate of 5.24% where the Filed Plan has none.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Connects interest to feasibility concerns from ISSUE_007
criteria_results.reasoning: It includes the $0.37M of interest in the Year-1 liquidity shortfall of (5.57) and in the feasibility screen.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies supplemental disclosure condition precedent
criteria_results.reasoning: B-3 identifies the new ED condition § 9.1(g), which requires a court-approved supplemental disclosure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Flags timeline delay risk to Effective Date
criteria_results.reasoning: It discusses post-confirmation hold-up and vacatur leverage, but never ties the condition to delaying the Aug. 15 Effective Date and never mentions consequences such as DIP timelines or administrative costs.

criteria_results.title: Report includes an executive summary
criteria_results.reasoning: Section I is a labeled Executive Summary at the start.

criteria_results.title: Executive summary includes prioritized list for May 28 meet-and-confer
criteria_results.reasoning: The Executive Summary's numbered recommended posture is framed for the May 26/28 exchange. Section IX gives the May 28 trade plan and a numbered response matrix.

criteria_results.title: Each substantive change includes Accept/Reject/Negotiate recommendation
criteria_results.reasoning: Every substantive change has an explicit Accept, Accept-Mod, Counter or Reject recommendation.
